title: Permission-surface mapper and IAM Conditions generator for private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a Terraform module and accompanying validation + health checks that generates least-privilege IAM role/policy artifacts for Private (VPC) deployments using fine-grained permission surface mapping and IAM Conditions where supported. The module should produce auditable JSON policy bundles, enforce access boundaries for cross-account roles, and include drift detection and upgrade-safe transforms to support automated upgrades of policy shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a 'permission_surface' input that maps service-specific actions to logical job roles and outputs Terraform-managed google_iam_policy / aws_iam_policy artifacts or equivalent for target cloud providers
Generated policies minimize broad wildcards and use IAM Conditions (e.g., resource.name, request.time, request.auth) where applicable to narrow scope
Module provides a 'policy_validator' subcommand (Terraform external or CI checker) that rejects policies with >5% wildcarded actions or missing resource constraints
Health-check Lambda/Cloud Function that scans live roles for drift against module canonical output and reports on Console dashboard and PagerDuty if critical bindings deviate
Upgrade path: module supports a safe policy migration plan (create replacement roles, dual-bind for 7 days, rotate consumers, delete old role) documented and automatable via optional lifecycle hooks
design_decisions: Canonicalize permission surface as a YAML manifest input; module compiles to provider-specific policy JSON via templates
Prefer IAM Conditions to scope permissions instead of adding more granular action lists when cloud provider supports conditions
Separate 'bind' stage (roles/policies created) from 'grant' stage (service accounts/identities granted roles) to enable safer rollouts
Drift detection will use a hashed canonical representation stored in an S3/GCS bucket; periodic reconciler compares live bindings to canonical hash
Expose a 'strict_mode' boolean to enforce deny-on-unknown-permission in CI vs permissive mode for legacy migrations
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge RFC + design doc, security review kickoff
Week 1: Implement Terraform module scaffold + templating layer, unit tests for policy compilation
Week 2: Integrate policy_validator as GitHub Action and Terraform external data source
Week 3: Deploy health-check function to staging, add Console alerting hook and PagerDuty rule
Week 4: Pilot with 2 internal teams (Console and Dedicated) using feature flag, collect feedback
Week 5: Enable dual-bind migration flow and begin gradual rollout to customers who opted in
testing_plan: Unit tests for permission_surface YAML -> policy JSON compilation (coverage target 95%)
Property-based tests that mutate permission_surface and assert compiled policy still enforces resource constraints
Integration tests deploying module to a sandbox VPC (AWS + GCP) and running drift detection
E2E test that performs a safe role rotation sequence to validate upgrade path
Security fuzzing and static analysis on generated policies to ensure no excessive wildcards
